category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your coworker from Columbus says the Big Ten is actually better now, and points at recent playoff results. Respond as an SEC fan. Hold the line.
response:
Listen, I’ll give credit where it’s due—congrats to the Big Ten on having a good year. But let’s be real for a second and look at the big picture. 

First of all, aren't you an Ohio State fan? You’re really going to point to *Michigan’s* national championship to prop up your conference? Down here in the SEC, we don't ride our rivals' coattails. 

Since the BCS era started and rolling right through the playoff era, the SEC has been the undisputed king of college football. You guys get one natty and suddenly the power dynamic has shifted? Before Michigan did it, Georgia went back-to-back. Before that, Alabama. Before that, LSU arguably had the greatest college football season of all time. We have *five* different programs that have won national titles since 2006 (Alabama, Georgia, LSU, Florida, Auburn). The Big Ten has two. 

It’s about depth, man. Top to bottom, your conference has a couple of heavyweights and a whole lot of filler. Surviving a November schedule in the SEC—going on the road to Death Valley at night, playing in Athens, dealing with a packed house at Neyland or Bryant-Denny—is a whole different animal than sleepwalking through a noon kickoff against Rutgers, Purdue, or Indiana. 

Look at the NFL draft every single April. The SEC produces the most draft picks, year in and year out, by a country mile. The talent disparity in the trenches isn't even a debate. 

So yeah, enjoy the recent hardware up in Ann Arbor. But one good playoff run doesn’t erase two decades of absolute dominance down South. If you want to be the best, you have to beat the best consistently. Until the Big Ten can run the gauntlet week in and week out like we do, the crown stays exactly where it is. 

It Just Means More. See you in January.
